0.long_answer: The autoimmune disease in question is Hashimoto's thyroiditis. This condition is characterized by chronic inflammation of the thyroid gland due to the immune system attacking its own tissue, leading to gradual destruction of the gland. Over time, as the thyroid hormone levels decrease (resulting in hypothyroidism), patients may experience several clinical signs, one of which is the loss of hair in the outer third of the eyebrows. This particular sign, known as Hertoghe sign, is a classic clinical feature associated with severe hypothyroidism commonly seen in Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
